detail.longDescription: “So far as I can tell, current agent tooling is built to reuse existing interaction patterns, rather than demand and expect agent-specific tooling to be built. While it’s true that many organizations are building and providing purpose-built tooling to support agentic interactions, the purpose is to support agent use, but there isn’t much about the tooling that makes it agent-specific. The existing purpose-built tooling for agents (skills and MCP servers) are wrappers around pre-existing interaction methods used by humans — documentation and APIs. Other tooling exists, like “computer use”, to quite literally use interfaces designed and built for humans first. Other tooling to support agentic use, like command-line interface (CLI) tools or software development kits (SDKs) serve to formalize and structure pre-existing interactions with APIs, thus providing a more structured interface for agents to use, but humans can easily use those tools too. So long as AI agents succeed at prompted tasks using the same tools as humans, it’s unlikely that we’ll see tooling built exclusively for agents. Given the current state of agent tooling, providing documentation content without the web would mean ignoring interfaces that are actively used by AI agents. Of course, that’s not the only issue with providing headless-only documentation.” https:// thisisimportant.net/posts/head less-docs/ # TechnicalWriting # SoftwareDocumentation # AI # AIAgents # MCP # WebMCP # InformationArchitecture # AgenticAI
